name: Steve Reich
hook: A composer who let two tape loops of a preacher drift out of step, and heard a new kind of music in the gap.
blurb: Steve Reich was born in New York in 1936. In 1965 he made 'It's Gonna Rain' from a 1964 recording of Brother Walter, a Pentecostal street preacher in Union Square, San Francisco. He played the same short loop on two Wollensak tape machines at once. Because the machines ran at slightly different speeds, the loops slowly drifted apart, a process called phasing, and made new rhythms and echoes. He then moved the same process to live players ('Piano Phase', 1967) and to large groups ('Music for 18 Musicians', ECM, 1978). He played in the 1964 premiere of Terry Riley's 'In C' and suggested its steady pulse. Brian Eno has said in lectures that hearing 'It's Gonna Rain' was his first taste of minimalism, the kind of music that led to ambient. The Orb's 'Little Fluffy Clouds' (1990) samples Pat Metheny's recording of Reich's 'Electric Counterpoint' (1987).

signatureTracks.title: It's Gonna Rain
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Two tape loops of one voice, drifting apart. Phasing, invented on two cheap tape recorders.
